comments.body:
## THE READ SIDE IS UP — Gerrit 1324. Stacked on 1319/1320, above 1311.

`get_parent_map` now reads a non-sub-task's parent from the "Epic Link" field as well as
`fields.parent`, closing the round trip 1311 left open.

**Discovery is SHARED, not duplicated** — the point of the ticket. 1311's lookup was inline inside
`set_parent`; it is now extracted to `_resolve_epic_link_field_id()` and BOTH `set_parent` and
`get_parent_map` call it. One discovery path, one cache, so the write side and the read side cannot
disagree about which field they mean. A second parallel lookup would have been the obvious shortcut
and the wrong one.

**A real regression was caught during the extraction, and it is worth recording.** The inline code
read `self._epic_link_field_id` as a bare attribute, which breaks for a transport built via
`__new__` — several existing pagination tests do exactly that, skipping `__init__`. Wiring
`get_parent_map` straight to the attribute turned 3 of them RED. Fixed with `getattr`/`setattr`
against the `_MISSING` default: same caching, tolerant of a skipped `__init__`. **1311 shipped this
latent** — it only ever ran through `set_parent`, whose callers all construct normally, so nothing
exercised it. Extending a cached attribute to a second caller is what exposed it.

**RED evidence, captured against the REBASED baseline** (`b301e7513d`) by stashing the change and
re-running — not against a stale base:
 * `test_epic_parent_is_read_back_from_the_epic_link_field` → `{'DC-10': None}`, expected `DC-1`
 * `test_field_discovery_failure_hits_the_same_degradation_contract` → `{'DC-14': 'DC-5'}`, expected `{}`
 * `test_discovery_is_shared_with_set_parent_not_duplicated` → `{'DC-15': None}`, expected `DC-1`

Reported honestly by the implementer: **4 of the 7 cells passed trivially pre-fix** — they assert
behaviour that was already incidentally true. Those four are weak and should not be counted as
evidence; the three above are what discriminate.

Gates: ruff clean, mypy 421, hygiene 0, **2105 unit tests pass**, module-size contract passes.

### FLAGGED — `transport.py` is at 799/800

One line of headroom. This is now the THIRD time this file has forced prose-trimming to fit
(780 → 794 → 781 → 799 across 1302, 1305, 1311 and this change), and the next parent-related change
cannot land without a split. Per this epic's own precedent — b586 hit the same wall and was split
into a mechanical relocation (S1) followed by the policy change (S2), and S1 passed plan review
FIRST TRY where the combined ticket had taken ten rounds — the split should be its own change,
BEFORE more work lands here. Not filed unilaterally; recorded for the operator, since it is a
restructuring of a file three in-flight changes touch.

### STILL NOT PROVEN

That the read actually works against DC 8.17.1 — AC3 requires a harness run, and AC4's idempotence
question (does a converged epic-parent pair stop re-emitting?) is exactly the churn risk this
ticket was filed with. Neither is settled by 2105 green unit tests; 1276, 1288 and 1302 all had
that and were all wrong live.

## THE READ SIDE IS LIVE-PROVEN — run 30867072561, and the proof comes from an unexpected cell.

`get_parent_map` reading the Epic Link is confirmed against a real DC instance, and the evidence is stronger than a dedicated cell would have given. `test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips` reports:

    the DC Epic Link was cleared (confirmed absent from BOTH the direct GET and the
    SEARCH-BACKED PARENT MAP, WHICH 9bb9 TAUGHT TO READ IT)

That is this ticket's change doing its job on a live instance: the search-backed `get_parent_map` now tracks the Epic Link field, agrees with the direct GET, and does so through the shared `_resolve_epic_link_field_id()` discovery rather than a second parallel lookup.

The write side is proven in the same run — `test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link` executes and passes for the first time (see [rebar:3fe5-c22e-dc2d-4c9e]). So **the round trip closes end to end**: outbound writes the Epic Link, inbound reads it back.

### AC status

- [x] `get_parent_map` returns a non-sub-task's parent from the instance-discovered Epic Link
- [x] the two shapes do not collide — the sub-task cells still exercise `fields.parent` and fail on the PLATFORM no-op ([rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda]), not on being rerouted to the Epic Link
- [x] the round trip closes: a parent WRITTEN by outbound is SEEN by the next inbound read
- [x] degradation contract preserved (unit-pinned; unchanged by this run)
- [x] `transport.py` under the 800-LOC cap — comfortably: 465d split it to **230 lines** across five mixins, and `get_parent_map` now lives in `_hierarchy.py` (199)
- [ ] idempotence: repeated passes over a converged epic-parent pair emit NO further mutation

**Only idempotence is left, and I am not ticking it from this run.** The epic-parent cell passing proves ONE pass converges; it does not prove a SECOND pass is quiet. That is a distinct property and this epic has been burned four times by treating an adjacent green as evidence for a claim it does not make.

### A REAL FINDING this cell surfaced, which is NOT this ticket's

The same cell then fails: the Epic Link is gone remotely, but `.parent_id` locally is still set. The remote clear works and the read sees it — the local side does not follow. Recorded on [rebar:37e7-d751-0042-4b94], which owns that cell.

comments.body:
## AC6's CELL IS WRITTEN — Gerrit 1342. The existing idempotence cell does NOT cover it.

I checked before writing rather than assuming, and the gap is real: `test_a_repeat_pass_over_a_converged_pair_plans_nothing` converges a **title edit on a plain task**. Idempotence is a property of the WRITER and the READER agreeing about one field's value, so a summary proving quiet says nothing about a parent — the epic parent is written outbound as the Epic Link custom field and read back inbound by `get_parent_map`'s Epic Link branch, the two halves this ticket built. If they disagree, every pass re-emits the same attach and the store churns forever.

`test_a_repeat_pass_over_a_converged_epic_parent_plans_nothing` converges an epic-parent pair through a real pass, confirms the attach landed **by raw REST**, then **waits on `get_parent_map`** — the production read, not a direct GET — before re-planning. That wait is what makes a subsequent non-empty plan attributable to churn rather than index lag; without it the cell cannot tell the two apart.

Kept as a SEPARATE cell from the emit one, per this module's own recorded lesson: bundling idempotence into round-trip cells is what buried the real signal under thirteen false reds on J11's first run.

AC6 stays UNTICKED until it runs green. Round-2 (30870845838) predates it.

compiled_state.description:
# DC parent sync is ONE-WAY: outbound writes the Epic Link, inbound never reads it

## The asymmetry

After Gerrit **1311** (ticket 39c1), `JiraDataCenterTransport.set_parent` writes a non-sub-task's
parent to the instance-discovered "Epic Link" custom field. Nothing reads it back.

`get_parent_map` (`transport.py:515-546`) — the ONLY inbound parent read — searches with
`fields="parent"` and extracts `fields.parent` alone:

    for issue in self._paged_search(query, fields="parent", rate_limit_retry=True):
        parent = fields.get("parent") if isinstance(fields, dict) else None
        out[key] = parent.get("key") if isinstance(parent, dict) else None

Repo-wide, `Epic Link` / `_epic_link` appears ONLY in `transport.py`'s outbound path.

**So a parent rebar sets on Data Center is invisible to rebar on the next inbound pass.** On DC,
inbound can only ever see a SUB-TASK's parent — and [rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda] gives reason to doubt
even that path takes effect.

## Why this is the epic's signature class, again

"Cloud has the translation, DC never got its half" — d067, 8d68, 751e, 2b16/88d9, 39c1. This is a
fresh instance, created by the fix for the sixth one. Not a regression (nothing read the Epic Link
before), and 1311 is not wrong — its scope was the outbound half, and the emit gate only ever emits
an EPIC parent, so the Epic Link is the correct target. But the ROUND TRIP is open, and epic e369's
headline criterion is BIDIRECTIONAL reconcile.

## The unproven risk that makes this more than cosmetic

If outbound writes a parent the next inbound pass cannot see, the differ may re-emit the SAME parent
mutation every pass — the perpetual re-emission bug 8b25 was filed for (~230 steady-state
`fields=['parent']` mutations on Cloud). **Explicitly NOT asserted here**: it depends on how the
outbound differ decides a parent is already synced. The live cell that would show it is
`test_a_repeat_pass_over_a_converged_pair_plans_nothing`, which is currently GREEN — so either the
churn does not occur or that cell does not cover this shape. Settle it before assuming either.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `get_parent_map` returns a non-sub-task's parent from the instance-discovered "Epic Link"
      field, in addition to `fields.parent` for sub-tasks — field id discovered BY NAME, never
      hardcoded, reusing the discovery+cache the outbound side already has rather than a second copy
- [ ] the two shapes do not collide: a sub-task's `fields.parent` still wins where both exist, and a
      test pins which takes precedence
- [ ] the round trip closes: a parent WRITTEN by outbound is SEEN by the next inbound read, asserted
      against a real DC instance on a harness run (run id recorded). A unit suite does NOT settle
      this — changes 1276, 1288 and 1302 were all mutation-proven and all wrong live
- [ ] idempotence is proven, not assumed: repeated passes over a converged epic-parent pair emit NO
      further parent mutation — this is the churn risk above
- [ ] `get_parent_map`'s degradation contract is preserved: a failure still logs a WARNING and
      returns `{}` so the inbound pass falls back to parentless rather than aborting
- [ ] `transport.py` stays under the 800-LOC cap (it is ~781 after 1311; the discovery helper
      already exists, so this should reuse it rather than grow a parallel one)
